note.value: Elliptical flow can occur in a variety of geometric systems, such as around a vertical fracture, through an isotropic porous medium, and from an aquifer which has either an elliptical internal boundary or an isotropic permeability distribution. Therefore, the general treatment of elliptical flow can be an important problem in reservoir engineering. The transient flow theory and practice has been developed in detail for radial and linear systems; however, only a few solutions have been developed for elliptical flow. The knowledge on the subject is far from complete. The purpose of this study is to fill this existing gap in knowledge. For an elliptical inner boundary, it is not practical to solve the diffusivity equation in Cartesian coordinates. Hence, the diffusivity equation was transformed into elliptical coordinates. It is also shown that with proper variable transformation, this elliptical flow model can also be used for an anisotropic medium.For the case of constant-pressure at an elliptical inner boundary, the elliptical diffusivity equation was solved using Laplace transformation and separation of variables. To invert this solution, the Mellin transformation was used. This solution, in turn, was used to develop solutions for flow rate and cumulative production.For the case of the constant-producing rate, the above solution technique cannot be used. Instead, the analytical solution was developed by using superposition. The cumulative production solution was superposed in time to obtain a constant-rate solution.Because these analytical solutions were in the form of infinite integrals and accurate evaluation of these integrals was difficult, a numerical Laplace transform inversion technique was used to develop tables and curves useful for pressure analysis.For the vertical fracture case, the long-time approximation was derived for the case of the constant-flow rate. It was shown that the existing stead-state approximation of elliptical flow for long times is valid for both unsteady-state elliptical and anisotropic flow. Appropriate time limits for the long-time approximation are presented for different a/b ratios (where a/b is the ratio of the major and minor axes of the internal boundary ellipse).Effective well radii for different a/b ratios and boundary conditions were developed based on this long-time approximation. The effective well radius for elliptical flow was found to be independent of whether the reservoir is producing at a constant-flow rate or a constant-pressure and is independent of whether the reservoir has an isotropic or anisotropic permeability distribution.The results of this study are presented in formats suitable for application to transient pressure analysis for anisotropic and vertically fractured reservoirs. Type-curves were also developed to compute water influx from an aquifer which has either an elliptical inner boundary or an anisotropic permeability distribution.
Kucuk, Fikri. (1978). Transient Flow in Elliptical Systems. Stanford Digital Repository. Available at: https://purl.stanford.edu/yj054pw8531
